title: Why food spoils, and how to start processing safely

say: Why food spoils, and how to start processing safely.
This is the video for Module 1 of Small-Scale Food Processing.
At harvest time, tomatoes, pepper, plantain and cassava arrive in huge quantities. Prices crash, and a lot of food goes bad before it is sold.

say: Fresh food spoils for three main reasons. First, microorganisms: bacteria, moulds and yeasts feed on the moisture and nutrients in food.
They need water, food, warmth and time. Every method you learn takes away at least one of these.

cards.d: Bacteria, moulds and yeasts feed on the moisture and nutrients in food.
Enzymes inside the food keep working after harvest, softening and browning it.
Insects, rodents and bruising open the door to both.

say: Water is the most important factor. Properly dried foods keep. Dried pepper should snap, not bend. Garri should flow freely. Chips should crunch, not chew.
If a product bends or feels leathery, there is still enough water for mould.

panel.heading: How processing stops spoilage
items: Water: dry it until it snaps or crunches
Heat: kills microbes and stops enzymes
Acid: slows bacteria, like sour garri
Salt and sugar: bind the water

say: Heat, from roasting or frying, kills most microorganisms. But once food cools and is exposed again, only good packaging protects it.

say: Acid slows bacteria. Fermented garri becomes slightly sour, which helps it keep.

say: Garri shows the science clearly. Cassava contains natural compounds that can release cyanide, and each step has a job.
Peel and wash within a day or two of harvest, because the roots rot fast.

panel.heading: How cassava becomes garri
items: Peel and wash within a day or two
Grate into a fine mash
Bag, ferment and press, 1 to 3 days
Sieve the pressed cake
Roast on steady heat, stirring
Cool fully, sieve and pack

say: Grate into a fine mash. This lets the natural enzymes start breaking down the cyanide compounds.

say: Bag, ferment and press, usually for one to three days. The liquid drains out and takes some cyanide with it.

say: Sieve the cake to remove fibre and lumps.

say: Roast in a wide pan on steady heat, stirring constantly until dry and crisp.

say: Cool fully before packing, because packing warm causes mould.
For example, Bisi pressed for only half a day and roasted on high heat. Her garri went lumpy and stale. Next time she pressed for two full days and roasted on medium heat.

panel.rule: Never rush pressing or roasting: water and cyanide stay behind.

say: Adding value means the finished product earns more than everything you spent, not just the raw food.
Ngozi buys 10 plantain fingers for about 2,500 naira, and needs about 1,500 naira of frying oil.
Gas is about 500 naira, and 20 pouches with labels about 1,000 naira.
Her batch costs about 5,500 naira, or about 275 naira a pack. At 400 naira a pack, 20 packs bring in about 8,000 naira.
That leaves about 2,500 naira for her time and profit. Worth testing with one small batch first.
Hot oil causes serious burns. If oil catches fire, turn off the gas if you can do so safely, cover the pot with a lid or fire blanket, and leave it covered until cool.
Keep children away from the frying area, and check gas hoses with soapy water.

panel.heading: Hot oil and gas safety
left: Turn off the gas if safe
Cover the pot with a lid
right: Check for leaks with a flame
Bottle pepper in oil at home

say: Never leave frying oil unattended. Never pour water on burning oil: it explodes into a fireball. Never check for leaks with a flame.
And never seal pepper, garlic or vegetables in oil at home. That can grow a deadly toxin you cannot see, smell or taste.

panel.heading: Hot oil and gas safety
left: Turn off the gas if safe
Cover the pot with a lid
right: Check for leaks with a flame
Bottle pepper in oil at home

say: Your space must flow one way: receive, wash, process, cool, pack, store. Food never moves back from clean to dirty. If space is tight, do raw work first, then clean the surfaces.
Wash hands with soap often, cover your hair and cuts, and do not handle food when sick.

panel.heading: A safe, clean space on a small budget
items: Food moves one way: raw to packed
Separate dirty and clean work
Wash hands with soap and running water
Cover hair; cover cuts
No handling food when sick
Store off the floor, safe from rats

say: To remember. Food spoils through microbes, enzymes and pests. Dry until it snaps or crunches. Never skip a garri step. Never pour water on an oil fire.
And start with one product, chosen for access, equipment, safety and demand.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Food spoils through microbes, enzymes and pests
Dry until it snaps or crunches
Every garri step cuts cyanide or moisture
Never pour water on an oil fire
Choose one first product, on purpose
